{{short description|Italian mathematician (born 1963)}}
{{use dmy dates|date=February 2026}}
[[File:Susanna Terracini.jpg|thumb|Terracini in 2020 or earlier]]
'''Susanna Terracini''' ({{IPA|it|suˈzanna terraˈtʃiːni}}; born 29 April 1963){{r|cv}} is an Italian mathematician known for her research on [[Chaos theory|chaos]] in [[Hamiltonian system|Hamiltonian dynamical system]]s, including the [[n-body problem|''n''-body problem]], [[reaction–diffusion system]]s, and the [[Schrödinger equation]].{{r|ewm}}

== Life and career ==
Terracini was born in [[South London]]{{r|cv}} to a distant cousin of Italian [[anti-fascist]] politician [[Umberto Terracini]].{{r|manifesto}} She earned a ''[[laurea]]'' in 1986 in mathematics at the [[University of Turin]], supervised by Fulvia Skof.{{r|cv}}
She completed her Ph.D. at the [[International School for Advanced Studies]] in 1990. Her dissertation, ''Periodic Solutions to Singular Newtonian Systems'', was supervised by [[Ivar Ekeland]] and Sergio Solimini.{{r|cv|mgp}}

She was a researcher at [[Paris Dauphine University]] from 1988 to 1989, and became a faculty member at the [[Polytechnic University of Milan]] in 1990. In 2001 she became a full professor at the [[University of Milano-Bicocca]], and in 2012 she returned to Turin as a professor.{{r|cv}} {{as of|2026|2|post=,}} Terracini is a member of the Scientific Advisory Board of the Barcelona [[Centre de Recerca Matemàtica]].{{r|crm}}

== Awards and recognition ==
One of Terracini's papers on the [[n-body problem|''n''-body problem]] was selected for a featured review in ''[[Mathematical Reviews]]''.{{r|ewm|chen}}
She was the winner of the 2002 [[Vinti Prize]], a prize of the [[Italian Mathematical Union]] for young researchers in [[mathematical analysis]]. In 2007 she won the Bruno Finzi Prize of the [[Istituto Lombardo Accademia di Scienze e Lettere]].{{r|ewm}} 
In 2020 she was awarded the Schauder Medal from the Juliusz P. Schauder Center for Nonlinear Studies at the [[Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń]], Poland.{{r|schm}}

== Positions on other issues ==
In early 2024, amid [[Gaza war|Israel's war on Gaza]], Terracini was the only member of the [[academic senate]] at Turin to vote against [[academic boycott of Israel|severing ties with Israeli institutions]], declaring herself opposed to academic boycotts by principle and stating dialogue should always be favoured; she had previously opposed the suspension of agreements with Russian universities during the [[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|war on Ukraine]].{{r|manifesto}} She later criticized [[Gaza war protests at universities|student protesters]] for their vocal [[anti-Zionist]] stance which, according to her, was due to the blind adoption of a [[Hamas]] narrative.{{r|stampa}}
